text:
maya: Quick check — after shading our Kotlin SDK into the app fat-jar I'm getting NoClassDefFoundError: okhttp3.internal.Platform when starting streaming requests. Using Gradle Shadow relocate for most deps. Anyone hit this?

ryan: Yep, saw similar. My rule of thumb: do NOT relocate OkHttp internals. OkHttp relies on package-private/internal refs that break if relocated. Instead either ship OkHttp unshaded or use the provider artifact.

maya: Ah — do you mean exclude okhttp from the shadowJar entirely?

ryan: Exactly. In build.gradle:
```groovy
shadowJar {
  dependencies {
    exclude(dependency('com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp'))
  }
}
```
Or keep okhttp on the classpath as a separate artifact.

oliver: Another angle: double-check Jackson/Gson clashes. We had weird serializer errors after shading two different jackson-databind versions. Best to align versions via BOM or avoid relocating jackson packages unless you relocate everything consistently.

maya: Good call — the stacktrace also showed com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.exc.InvalidDefinitionException in some flows.

sophia: For Kotlin specifically, prefer jackson-module-kotlin or Moshi with Kotlin adapters. For Jackson:
```kotlin
val mapper = jacksonObjectMapper()
  .registerModule(KotlinModule())
  .configure(DeserializationFeature.FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES, false)
```
That avoids a bunch of "no constructor"/missing parameter issues.

oliver: If you must use Gson, watch out: Gson doesn't respect Kotlin non-null by default; use custom TypeAdapters or consider Moshi (with KotlinJsonAdapterFactory).

maya: Streaming quirks — any OkHttp tips? The app hangs if the server streams and we call .string() elsewhere.

ryan: For streaming responses don't call response.body?.string() — that buffers the entire body. Use the source() or byteStream() and process incrementally:
```kotlin
response.body?.byteStream()?.use { input ->
  val reader = BufferedReader(InputStreamReader(input))
  reader.lineSequence().forEach { line ->
    // handle chunk
  }
}
```
Also set call/connect/read timeouts appropriately (streaming can be long lived):
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .connectTimeout(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) // 0 = no timeout for streaming reads
  .callTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
  .build()
```

oliver: And add an EventListener to log DNS/connection events if you're seeing unexpected reconnects.

sophia: On shading jackson: if your app (or other libs) bring an older jackson, prefer BOM to unify versions. If you must relocate, do it like: relocate 'com.fasterxml.jackson', 'shaded.com.fasterxml.jackson' (but then all code using jackson has to reference relocated packages).

maya: Helpful. I'll try excluding okhttp from the shadow and align jackson versions. If still broken I'll paste our shadow config.

oliver: Here's a minimal working shadow snippet we used:
```groovy
shadowJar {
  relocate 'com.google.common', 'shaded.com.google.common'
  // intentionally NOT relocating okhttp or com.fasterxml.jackson.*
  dependencies {
    exclude(dependency('com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp'))
  }
}
```

ci-bot: Deployed artifact-20260308-42 with exclude-okhttp change to staging.

maya: Nice — thanks all. Will test streaming and report back. :thumbsup:
